title: Intel 18A yields hit 70%, signs Xeon+EMIB LTA with Microsoft
gist: Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan says 18A yields have reached 70% (likely functional yield) — reasonable for this stage of the Panther Lake/Clearwater Forest ramp — and Intel signed a long-term deal with Microsoft securing multi-year Xeon supply (incl. Diamond Rapids) and making Microsoft the first company to publicly commit to EMIB packaging for in-house silicon.

insights.claim: Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan said yields on Intel's 18A (1.8nm-class) process have reached 70%, up from 'horrible' when he took over in March 2025.
insights.speaker: Anton Shilov
insights.so_what: 18A yield progress de-risks Intel Foundry's roadmap and margins; a key INTC datapoint.
insights.quote: When I took over [as CEO in March, 2025], 18A yield was horrible; now we are at 70%

insights.claim: Lip-Bu Tan did not specify whether the 70% 18A figure was functional yield, parametric yield, or sellable silicon; it most likely refers to functional die yield.
insights.speaker: Anton Shilov
insights.so_what: Headline yield numbers are ambiguous; economics depend on the parametric/sellable mix not disclosed.

insights.claim: A 70% functional yield on 18A is roughly in line with expectations for an all-new process at this stage of its ramp, since Panther Lake compute tiles entered volume production in the second half of 2025.
insights.speaker: Anton Shilov
insights.so_what: Signals 'on track' rather than a breakthrough — temper expectations of a step-change in Intel economics.

insights.claim: Intel's 18A economics depend heavily on parametric yield and how many premium high-bin Core Ultra 300 'Panther Lake' SKUs it can supply, rather than functional yield alone.
insights.speaker: Anton Shilov
insights.so_what: Watch Panther Lake premium SKU availability and gross margin as the real yield signal.

insights.claim: Intel's Xeon 6+ Clearwater Forest, with up to 288 cores, is in high-volume production using 18A compute chiplets and Foveros Direct 3D stacking.
insights.speaker: Anton Shilov
insights.so_what: Shows 18A is shipping in data center products, not just client.
insights.locator: The same applies to Intel's Xeon 6+

insights.claim: Microsoft signed a long-term agreement with Intel securing multi-year Xeon supply capacity, including next-generation Xeon 'Diamond Rapids', though purchase volumes and financial terms were not disclosed.
insights.speaker: Anton Shilov
insights.so_what: Improves Intel's server CPU demand visibility; adds evidence of Microsoft hedging x86 supply.
insights.locator: In addition to announcing an important 18A milestone

insights.claim: Microsoft is the first company to publicly commit to Intel's EMIB advanced packaging for its own multi-chiplet data center silicon, which the author calls arguably the biggest news for Intel Foundry — though not necessarily the first third-party EMIB user.
insights.speaker: Anton Shilov
insights.so_what: A named external packaging customer validates Intel Foundry's advanced packaging as an alternative to TSMC CoWoS-type capacity.
insights.quote: The EMIB agreement is arguably the biggest news.

insights.claim: The Microsoft–Intel EMIB announcement does not identify the processors, process node, volumes or deployment schedule, and it is unclear whether it relates to Microsoft's 2024 commitment to use 18A for data center silicon.
insights.speaker: Anton Shilov
insights.so_what: Revenue impact for Intel Foundry is unquantified; wait for volume/timing disclosures.
insights.locator: However, the announcement does not identify

insights.claim: Because most high-end data center chips use multi-chiplet designs, Microsoft's future in-house data center processors are reasonably expected to use EMIB for multi-die integration.
insights.speaker: Anton Shilov
insights.so_what: Implies potentially recurring packaging business for Intel across Microsoft silicon generations.
insights.locator: As the majority of high-end data center solutions

insights.claim: Intel Foundry's Naga Chandrasekaran framed the EMIB deal as combining heterogeneous integration flexibility with manufacturing scale to advance future generations of Azure infrastructure.
insights.speaker: Anton Shilov
insights.so_what: Intel pitching packaging + scale as its foundry differentiator for hyperscaler custom silicon.
insights.quote: combine the flexibility of heterogeneous integration with the manufacturing scale required for the AI era
insights.locator: Through use of our advanced packaging capabilities

insights.claim: Intel and Microsoft are jointly developing infrastructure capabilities spanning processor architecture, heterogeneous integration, CXL memory expansion, QuickAssist Technology acceleration and Trust Domain Extensions security.
insights.speaker: Anton Shilov
insights.so_what: Deeper co-development than a supply deal increases switching costs in Azure's x86 fleet.
